name: Loyalty
title: Loyalty: operator and guest paths and what can go wrong

BANDS.s: Loyalty switched on for the restaurant, access to the Loyalty pages in Web Dash
Operator builds tiers: a points threshold, a name and the free menu items it unlocks
Which channels may check out with a reward and the per-order redemption limits
The cached loyalty menu that POS, mPOS, Kiosk, CFD and Online ordering read
How a guest becomes a loyalty member on each channel and how profiles are matched
Points worked out on the ticket and credited when it is fully paid, plus late assignment
Balance shown, reward picked, limits checked and points deducted on each channel
Void, full refund, partial refund, cancellation and repayment of a loyalty ticket
Loyalty Overview KPIs, activity list and the guest profile in the Guest Book
Tier changes after launch and turning the programme off
Loyalty 2.0 and release 9.0 changes described in PRDs, not live yet

NODES.d: A restaurant can reward identified guests with points from eligible paid tickets. The earn rate is 100 points per eligible dollar. Guests can spend points on configured reward items.
e: Restaurant expects a configurable earn rate, points expiry or sign-up bonus that the product does not offer

NODES.d: The restaurant level loyalty switch is turned on (by AIO onboarding or Ops). Every earn path, the online and Kiosk reward menus and post payment redemption check this switch; with it off, tickets earn 0 points.
e: Switch left off after onboarding, tickets earn 0 points and nothing is credited later
Guests lose points for every order
Switch turned on but no tier created, guests earn points with nothing to spend them on
Switch state cached by devices and backend, a change is not picked up until the cache refreshes
Multi-location brand enables loyalty on one location only, a guest earns in one store and sees 0 in another

NODES.d: The operator opens Marketing, Loyalty, with an Overview tab and a Configure tab, scoped to the selected location. One permission covers all of Loyalty; any role with access can change tiers and settings.
e: Any role with Loyalty access can create, change or delete tiers and limits, no finer permission
Backend loyalty endpoints take the restaurant ID from the request, a user of one location could read or change another location of the tenant

NODES.d: On Configure the operator adds a tier with a name and a points value. The points value is a whole number of at least 500 and must be unique among active tiers of the location; the backend rejects a duplicate with Tier already exist.
e: Tier names are free text and not unique, two tiers with the same name confuse staff and reports
Two managers create a tier with the same points at the same time, uniqueness is checked before the write with no database constraint
Points threshold set very low or very high by a typo, no confirmation of the dollar equivalent
Duplicate points error shown as a generic toast
Operator does not know what to fix

NODES.d: The operator searches menu items and adds 1 to 25 items to the tier. An item can belong to only one active tier; the backend checks the items exist for this location and are not used by another tier.
e: Item already used by another tier is rejected only at save, without naming the tier
Inactive, hidden or out of stock item can be picked, reward later invisible on Online ordering and Kiosk
Reward line stores no menu ID or category ID, redeemed items drop out of the menu report
High priced item put in a low tier by mistake, nothing shows its price against the points
Item search lists the same item once with no menu context, wrong variant picked

NODES.d: For each item the operator may pin one size option and pick modifier options that are free with the reward. Other priced modifiers the guest adds are charged. Each modifier needs at least one option selected.
e: Item with a required size saved without a size, devices pick a size or block the reward differently
Free modifier options charged on one channel and free on another (old single size column and new modifier tables both read)
Nested modifier options configured as free are matched by ID on POS against a stale local menu
Modifier option later deleted in Menu Manager, reward still points at it

NODES.d: The tier, its items and their modifiers are written in one transaction. If the new top tier is above the per-order points limit, the limit is raised to match; it is never lowered here. The cached loyalty menu is cleared.
e: Points limit raised automatically without telling the operator, guests can now redeem more per order
More value given away than intended
A register misses the menu refresh after a tier is saved
The cashier still sees the previous rewards until the menu refreshes
Save fails part way, transaction rolls back but the form shows success from an earlier response

NODES.t: Set checkout with reward per channel
NODES.d: General settings hold one switch per channel (POS, Online, Kiosk, mPOS, QR) allowing an order made only of reward items to be checked out. Defaults are on when the restaurant has no settings row yet.
e: Kiosk reads a missing settings row as off while every other channel reads it as on
Kiosk blocks reward only orders others allow
Switch label unclear, operator thinks it turns redemption off for the channel
An open register has not refreshed after the restaurant changes reward-only checkout settings
Staff may see a different checkout option from the one the restaurant just saved

NODES.d: Per order limits: points (default 500) and reward items (default 1), each with an Unlimited option. Both limits apply together; a reward is blocked if either would be exceeded. Saved only when the operator presses Save. The settings form validates a finite points limit against the most expensive active tier.
e: A cached settings screen uses a tier cost that another manager just raised
A reward can exceed the saved checkout limit
Two managers edit settings at once, last save wins with no warning
Deleting the last tier resets both limits to defaults without notice

NODES.d: The backend caches reward tiers and item details by location. Successful writes on covered loyalty and menu screens invalidate that cache. The register also keeps a local copy until it receives a refresh or reloads the menu.
e: A menu change reaches the backend but the register still has the previous version open
Staff can offer a reward whose modifiers or availability have changed
Heavily configured location exceeds the query timeout, menu returns an error and rewards disappear
Waiting requests give up after the lock wait and get an error during peak

NODES.d: Android POS fetches the restaurant reward menu, limits and customer-display timeout. It combines those settings with the attached guest balance and rewards already on the ticket. Kiosk has a dedicated loyalty menu. Online ordering filters its reward list by menu visibility and hours.
e: Kiosk shows only the loyalty menu and not the main menu
Online list hides rewards whose menu is outside its hours while POS still offers them
A reward appears selectable on one register after the guest or the ticket was updated on another
Staff may promise a reward before the updated balance or limits appear

NODES.d: Staff look up or add a guest by phone and attach the profile to the POS ticket. The loyalty menu uses the attached guest balance. A guest can also be identified on the customer-facing display.
e: Wrong number typed, points credited to a stranger
The cashier completes payment before confirming which profile is attached
The intended guest may need help claiming the points
Same guest exists twice (phone and online account), balance split across profiles
The name shown for a phone lookup does not match the guest at the register
Staff need to verify the profile before applying a reward

NODES.d: After a card payment the backend matches the card fingerprint (Adyen) to an existing profile. A signed-up guest on the ticket always wins; a guest profile found on the card is merged into them and both balances are added. Otherwise the card owner or a new guest is used.
e: Shared family or company card merges two people into one profile
A delayed card match finishes after staff have already attached a guest
Check that the ticket has one owner and its points appear once
An unidentified guest pays in cash and staff do not attach a profile
Card matching cannot identify the intended loyalty account
The payment succeeds but card matching fails
The guest may need support to locate the points

NODES.d: On Online ordering the guest signs in with phone and code. Rewards and points are shown only to signed-in guests; points are kept per location.
e: Online account and POS phone profile not linked, guest sees 0 points online
Guest orders as a guest checkout and earns nothing, no prompt to join
Brand with several locations shows a different balance per location without saying so

NODES.d: On the Kiosk the guest enters a phone number to look up or create a profile, before or after ordering. A new profile is created with 0 points and source Kiosk.
e: Anyone can type another guest's phone and see their balance and rewards
Typo creates a new empty profile instead of finding the real one
The kiosk verification code step adds friction for a guest who wants to continue ordering
The restaurant requests a simpler ordering experience

NODES.d: When moving from another loyalty system, the operator imports a guest file with points. Imported points are added to any existing balance for that guest at this location and set lifetime points.
e: Same file imported twice adds the points twice
Old system points at a different rate imported as is, value changes
Phone format differs, imported guest not matched to existing profile

NODES.t: Work out points on the ticket
NODES.d: Each ticket stores points earned: the discounted subtotal before tax, rounded to the cent, times 100. Tips, tax and reward items (priced at 0) do not earn. For tax inclusive restaurants the base is the tax inclusive original price.
e: A discounted tax-inclusive ticket uses its original tax-inclusive price as the earn base
The points can exceed what the guest expects from the discounted subtotal
A fractional-cent discount is rounded differently across channels
The guest can see a one-point difference for an otherwise equivalent order
A ticket includes gift card value or a service charge and the displayed earn amount is unclear
Staff cannot explain which part of the bill earned points
Earn rate fixed at 100 per dollar, cannot be set per restaurant or item

NODES.d: The payment completes on POS, mPOS, Kiosk or Online ordering and the ticket becomes fully paid. Payment webhooks trigger guest matching and the points update.
e: A completed payment reaches loyalty processing late or fails there
The guest can pay successfully before the points appear
A gift card covers part of the bill and the final tender is collected, but the ticket still shows partially paid
Points remain pending after the guest has paid in full
Split payments settle separately and the final settlement does not reach loyalty processing
The completed ticket can still show pending points

NODES.d: For each fully paid ticket the backend applies any redemption and earnings to the guest balance. It can record activity earlier with a partially paid status. A fully paid update changes that activity to settled. A repeat of an already processed status skips that side of the transaction.
e: The guest had enough points when a reward was selected, but fewer remain when the paid ticket settles
The backend can record the full reward cost while deducting only the points still available
A report counts partially paid activity as settled before the guest pays the rest
Points history can appear to disagree with the available balance
After a Kiosk redemption has settled, an older partial-payment update is processed before another fully paid update
The recorded status could move backwards and allow the same reward to be deducted again. Check out-of-order delivery
Posting points creates a missing restaurant guest record without supplying a registration source
Guest Book may be unable to show how this guest joined at the location

NODES.d: A guest who was unidentified at checkout may be able to claim points after payment. The Kiosk post-order sign-in and the Android POS customer-display flow can identify a guest using the paid ticket. Availability depends on the checkout flow.
e: No way to give points to a guest after the order on some channels
A post-payment identification request refers to a different ticket than the guest just paid
Points may be assigned to the wrong guest

NODES.d: On Kiosk, post-order sign-in reassigns the ticket and checks the stored credit flag. Where points already went to a prior profile, the transfer flow reconciles the relevant balances and activity. On Android POS, customer-display sign-in sends the paid ticket ID to the backend.
e: After a Kiosk guest claims an order, the points do not move to the intended account
The guest misses points from a paid order
A transfer updates the ticket owner but fails before the guest balances and activity finish updating
Guest Book and the receipt identify different owners for the points
Two post-order updates overlap while the paid ticket is being reassigned
Verify that the destination of the transfer receives one credit
By the time the order is reassigned, the previous profile has already spent some of the points
Crediting the new profile in full can leave the combined balances too high

NODES.d: On a supported POS card payment the customer display can offer sign-up, show an existing guest prompt, or show a member their points. The member screen has three reward slots in total. Skip and the countdown end the flow. A redemption error is shown on the display.
e: CFD stuck or frozen on the loyalty points screen
Shared card shows another person's name and balance on the screen
All available rewards require modifier choices, so none qualify for the customer display
A guest who could redeem at the register has no reward to select on this screen

NODES.d: Android POS checks the attached guest balance, rewards already selected, stock, and the per-ticket points and item limits. A selected reward can be removed. Each channel also has a setting for a ticket made entirely of rewards.
e: Balance shown is stale because pending tickets are not reflected
Guest told they qualify then refused
The guest has enough points but the ticket has reached its item or points limit. Android POS can show the same insufficient-points message
The cashier cannot tell whether to remove another reward or check the guest balance

NODES.t: Select a reward at the register
NODES.d: On Android POS, staff select an eligible reward for the attached guest. The register adds it to the open ticket or opens modifier selection. The traced cashier flow does not prompt for a text code. The server also exposes text-code endpoints, but their presence does not establish an mPOS checkout step.
e: The cashier applies the reward while the wrong phone profile is attached
The intended guest keeps their points and another guest may be charged
An eligible reward needs a modifier choice and the cashier leaves that selection before finishing
The cashier can think the guest selected a reward that never reached the ticket
Two open tickets show the same guest balance before either settles
Each can appear eligible. Recheck the final points spent across both tickets
The register still shows a reward that has been disabled or removed since the menu loaded
Staff may need to refresh the menu and choose another item
Reward line on a split check moves to a guest who did not redeem

NODES.t: Redeem on the CFD after paying
NODES.d: The guest confirms one of the displayed rewards. Android POS blocks repeat taps while the request is pending. The server rechecks the programme, active reward, ticket limits and guest balance. On success it adds a reward line to the paid ticket and sends it to the kitchen.
e: Two different paid tickets submit rewards against the same guest balance at nearly the same time
Both may pass the balance check before either updates the balance
Reward printed on KDS but the item is out of stock
Points deducted but the KDS ticket not fired
Line added with no menu or category ID
The confirmation says the reward was added and previews the remaining points before the server approves it
If the server declines, the guest can see an error after reading what looked like a success message

NODES.d: The signed-in guest picks rewards from the loyalty menu. At cart preparation the reward identity, active tier, location, size match and limits are checked; points are deducted with a row lock when the order completes. Size is part of the configured reward match. Ordinary modifiers do not create a separate reward identity.
e: Reward changed or deleted while in the cart, order rejected at checkout
Size mismatch rejected with a generic message
Cash Kiosk orders lose menu and category IDs on the reward line

NODES.d: The signed-in guest opens Rewards, picks an unlocked reward and adds it to the cart. The server stamps the real tier points, checks quantity 1, each reward once, and both limits before payment, and again on a $0 checkout.
e: Reward kept in an abandoned cart, balance not reserved, spent elsewhere first
Points deducted but the reward line dropped from the order
Reward stacked with a deal or promo, discount applied to the free item
Priced modifiers on the reward charged with tax on the full item

NODES.d: The system records the points spent and the value of reward items on the ticket. The ordinary paid-ticket flow posts redemption and earnings at settlement. Kiosk completion records its own redemption and the fully paid handler recognises that entry. Customer-display redemption updates an already paid ticket.
e: Free item value not recorded consistently, reports cannot value redemptions
Redeem row and balance written in separate steps on the CFD path

NODES.d: The kitchen receives the reward item. Android POS receipts can show loyalty savings, points earned or redeemed, and current balance for an identified loyalty guest. A paid modifier can still add a charge to the reward item.
e: A receipt for an unidentified guest prints a placeholder customer name
The guest sees an unexpected name on the receipt
An enrolled guest has loyalty activity but the ticket receipt lacks the guest or points data needed to print it
The guest cannot reconcile the printed balance with the order

NODES.d: Staff can remove a reward from an open ticket. Android POS blocks removal on a partially paid ticket in the traced reward-menu flow. After payment, a refund or payment cancellation follows a different points-reversal flow.
e: After staff remove an unpaid reward, the menu still counts it toward the ticket limit
The guest cannot select a replacement even though the reward was removed
Item voided after the reward was applied leaves points spent on a voided line

NODES.d: On a full refund or cancellation, the backend locks the guest balance and reverses the earnings and redemptions still applied to this ticket. For a split payment, the final refund is recognised after all payments are fully refunded.
e: The guest has spent the points earned on the refunded ticket and the reversal would take the balance below zero
The refund history can show a negative ending balance while the account displays zero
A split-ticket refund stops after only some of its payment refunds settle
The redeemed points stay spent until the full refund settles
Errors are logged and swallowed, no retry

NODES.d: A partial refund reverses the earned share for the refund, capped at the points still applied to the ticket. Redeemed points are returned on a terminal reversal, such as a full-ticket refund.
e: Several partial refunds or different tenders produce a rounded points amount that is hard to reconcile against individual items
Support may need to compare refundable earnings with the points already reversed
A guest expects points back for a reward on a ticket that is only partly refunded
The guest can see the cash refund while the redemption remains on the account

NODES.d: If a cancelled ticket is paid again, the old Earned and Redeem rows are treated as reversed and the repayment is a new earn and redeem.
e: Same second timestamps make the reversal look older than the original, repayment skipped
A repaid ticket is settled after the guest balance or reward selection changed
Verify that only the new ticket amounts affect the guest balance

NODES.d: KPI cards for new sign-ups, returning guests, loyalty orders and loyalty sales with comparison to the previous period, a guest activity trend by day, week or month, top 5 rewards with total redemptions, and redemptions by platform. Dates follow the closeout time.
e: Returning guests are interpreted as guests who redeemed
A report excludes inactive reward items when reading historical redemptions
Refunded tickets drop out of KPIs after the fact

NODES.d: A paged list of guests who earned or redeemed in the period, searchable by name, email or phone and sortable by visits, spend, points available, earned and redeemed. The Guest Book profile shows points and tier name.
e: Earned column uses ticket totals, not the ledger, and disagrees with the balance
No manual adjustment of points from Web Dash
Tier shown is the highest tier the balance reaches, it drops after a redemption

NODES.d: Editing a tier preserves existing reward identities. Removed items are soft deleted. Re-adding the same item and size can restore its original row and preserve historical references. Confirm historic totals separately after deleting a tier.
e: Tier points raised while a reward is in a guest's cart
Guests saving for a deleted tier are not told

NODES.d: Turning loyalty off stops earning and hides reward menus. Balances stay and come back if it is turned on again.
e: Guests are not told and balances stay without expiry
A guest opens the customer-display reward menu before the programme is switched off and confirms afterward
The guest can still see the earlier offer, but the backend declines redemption once it sees the disabled programme

NODES.d: Guests earn and redeem; the operator reviews the Overview.
Loyalty 2.0: tiers can hold $ off or % off rewards on the whole check or one item, sharing the 25 reward cap; the items limit becomes a rewards limit.
e: Order with other discounts not defined, minimum spend checked before or after
Refunds and voids of discount rewards not covered by the PRD

NODES.d: The Loyalty 2.0 plan adds a sign-up reward and milestone alerts. The transactional welcome for enrollment or eligible imported points is a separate existing flow.
e: Sign-up reward granted twice on double submission
Text sent without valid consent or in quiet hours

NODES.d: Release 9.0: every reward line carries the menu and category it was picked through and a backfill fills past lines.
e: Backfill picks the wrong menu for items on several menus
Items added through POS search still lose their IDs after the release

NOTES: Where the restaurant loyalty switch is turned on and off (Super Admin or Ops) was not traced, so A2 and J2 are TBC

Android POS cashier and customer-display flows were read in android-pos internal at d2b5329. Kiosk and mPOS coverage here relies on backend contracts or linked field tickets. Their device interfaces were not tested.
Android POS selects a reward directly in the traced cashier flow. Text-code endpoints exist in Zeus, but a required or optional text-code step was not found in that Android POS path.
The earn rule is fixed in code: 100 points per dollar on the discounted pre-tax subtotal; tax inclusive restaurants use the tax inclusive original price
No points expiry, sign-up bonus, manual adjustment or liability report was found in the live code
Online ordering checks were read in the shared redemption helpers only; the online UI was not traced in detail
The full PROD 4848 description requests an optional verification code during kiosk ordering. It does not identify a reward redemption code or request removal of the loyalty menu.
Stage K is from the Loyalty 2.0 PRD (release not named) and the Menu and Category IDs PRD (release 9.0)
Zeus internal, 02473c3bac9. See features/loyalty/components/configure, marketing/loyalty/loyalty.service.ts and kiosk-loyalty-redemption.utils.ts.

Device check: open the reward menu, disconnect the POS and remove a tier from Web Dash. Check what staff can see or select while offline, then reconnect and verify the menu and guest points. Offline POS redemption has not been established. The backend post-payment redemption flow checks that the reward item is active and that the guest has enough points.

Evidence for F2 to H4: Zeus guest.service.ts (handleTicketLoyalty and handleRefundLoyaltyPoints), kiosk-loyalty-redemption.utils.ts, loyalty.service.ts (applyPostPaymentRedemption) and ticket.service.ts (handlePostOrderAuthKiosk). Android evidence: LoyaltyMenuUiModels.kt, LoyaltyMenuFragment.kt, LoyaltyMenuRepositoryImpl.kt, LoyaltyPointsSummarySecondaryScreen.kt, CFDPaymentLoyaltyRepoImpl.kt and TicketReceiptMapper.kt. Scenarios without a linked field ticket are QA checks, not observed incidents.

Customer-display insufficient points is a server rejection (HTTP 400) and a changed ticket limit is a conflict (HTTP 409). The Android success branch does not check a failure flag inside a successful HTTP response. A false success would require that different response contract. No such response was found for these current rejections.
